tools.install: winget install Git.Git   (Git for Windows; the probe is tested against it)
winget install Rustlang.Rustup   (then: rustup default stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)
winget install astral-sh.uv   (runs make_large_tree.py and extract_failures.py)
winget install NASM.NASM   (the aws-lc-sys crates in quarto-hub need it)
winget install Kitware.CMake   (the aws-lc-sys crates in quarto-hub need it)
Visual Studio Build Tools, "Desktop development with C++" (cargo finds link.exe itself, so absent from PATH is normal; install only if the build says "linker not found")
fnm/nvm; Node major per .nvmrc (items b1 to b7)
optional: winget install jj-vcs.jj (the jj scenarios of b1 skip without it)

items.title: build the test binaries for the four crates
git probe on Git for Windows
items.proves: rev-parse --git-path output with a drive letter (C:/...) and from a linked worktree parses; ls-tree -r -z with a project prefix returns the right paths; symlink entries (mode 120000) are filtered; cat-file --batch frames binary content correctly; reflog subjects parse.
items.does_not_prove: Any Git build other than Git for Windows, or colocated jj.

items.title: the gate during a real git switch of a 4,000-file tree
items.proves: The controller reports the gate closed for every real marker git creates during a switch of a large tree, and releases it afterward (six switches). The skip-never-delete behavior for an unreadable file is a hub behavior, covered by a5.
items.does_not_prove: Antivirus or OneDrive interplay, or timings on a cold cache.

items.title: core.autocrlf=true: classifier and arrival comparisons
items.proves: A CRLF-checked-out file compares equal to its blob content after normalization, through the classifier and the arrival comparison, for text; binaries compare by bytes.
items.does_not_prove: .gitattributes filters (LFS, ident), or the CRLF case if autocrlf was not true (the script marks that caveat).

items.title: paths and keys: registry keys and hub path_keys
items.caveat: core.longpaths is (unset), not true: git operations on paths over 260 characters may fail for reasons unrelated to the code.
items.proves: Registry keys use /; a case-insensitive collision of two keys falls back to ordinary sync; drive letters, UNC prefixes, and long paths (with core.longpaths) round-trip.
items.does_not_prove: NTFS 8.3 short names or Unicode normalization differences.

items.title: hub gate and checkpoint integration with a real repo
items.proves: The gate inside sync_all holds with a real repo; the checkpoint is written before the pointer flips; no code path renames a directory while it holds a handle in it; the unreadable-file test (an injected PermissionDenied, a skip and never a delete) passes on Windows. The injected error stands in for a real sharing violation; a real one needs a second process holding the file open.
items.does_not_prove: Network filesystems or Dev Drive behavior.

items.title: clippy -D warnings, four crates
items.proves: The epic's own gate is green on the Windows host target.
items.does_not_prove: Tests that need pandoc or typst unless -WithTools was given. Failures that also appear in the macOS baseline are listed as known unrelated in the plan notes.

items.title: clean root install, extension typecheck and bundle, ts-packages builds
items.proves: npm ci succeeded at the pinned Node; the extension typechecks (including e2e), its esbuild bundle builds, and every ts-packages workspace builds on Windows.
items.does_not_prove: vsce package; installing a .vsix; the hub-client and preview-SPA builds (they need the WASM and a pandoc download).

items.title: git probe, controller, and scenarios of the TypeScript package on Git for Windows
items.proves: The probe parses Git for Windows output (C:/... from --git-path, ls-tree -z quoting, reflog); the controller sees real index.lock and rebase-merge markers; the shared scenario step lists run against real repositories in %TEMP%. jj scenarios skip when jj is absent.
items.does_not_prove: Other Git builds; jj on Windows unless it is installed.

items.title: keys and paths: registry keys, ignore rules, safeJoin NTFS forms, junction, long path
items.proves: The TypeScript key normalization, ignore rules, and safeJoin hold for Windows path forms: / keys, drive letters and UNC prefixes, case collisions, nested .quarto-hub and .git segments, .git. and .git::$INDEX_ALLOCATION, a directory junction pointing outside the root, a path over 260 characters, and (where the volume has 8.3 names) GIT~1.
items.does_not_prove: Filesystems other than NTFS; Dev Drive or OneDrive behavior. The 8.3 row skips on a volume with short names disabled.

items.title: core.autocrlf=true: content rule, arrival, and the dirty check
items.proves: A CRLF checkout does not look dirty, and comparisons normalize as the macOS tests assume (the autocrlf-checkout scenario, arrival step 3, the origination dirty check).

items.title: extension core engine and headless peer: watcher, disk writes, rebind, atomic record write
items.proves: The engine runs on Windows: the injected watcher, writes to disk, rebind deleting the Automerge store after the repo is shut down (no EBUSY), and the atomic write of git-epochs.json retrying a rename refused with EPERM or EBUSY.
items.does_not_prove: VS Code's own file watcher; a real scanner or watcher holding the file (the EPERM test injects the error).

items.title: Join: q2 spawn through a stub q2.cmd, readiness, stdin close, tree kill, ticket hygiene
items.proves: Spawn and kill semantics on Windows: the ticket in argv, a free port, the readiness poll of the stub /health, stdin close ending the stub, kill of the whole process tree on Leave, stderr surfaced, no ticket in any log; .cmd is spawned through a shell.
items.does_not_prove: The iroh tunnel across real networks. The optional real q2 preview --share host and --join guest is not scripted: run it by hand if the network allows.

items.title: origination: offline publish, resume, second peer reads every file
items.proves: Publish order and resume on NTFS paths and Node file handles: docs and registry entries exist before the connect, the share link only after the heads are confirmed, an interrupted publish resumes from local storage, and a second peer reads every file.
items.does_not_prove: An out-of-process q2 hub (these tests run an in-process hub); the public server; very large uploads.

items.title: every a and b item together on the final code
items.reason: items did not run: a6 (with -SkipBuild a0 is absent)
items.proves: Nothing regressed on Windows after the fix plans: every a and b item ran in one invocation on the final code and is green together.
items.does_not_prove: Anything the items did not already cover.
